# Colecto v0.3.0

A redesigned Settings, background services on Linux, and a much bigger toolkit for
extensions: a message bus, owner settings, and a Rust SDK with its own build tool.

## Settings

- **Accounts** are compact rows with Reconnect, Edit and Remove buttons. Adding and
  editing happen in a dialog. Remove now deletes the account and its local data.
- **Appearance** offers five bundled fonts (Mona Sans, Inter, Geist, IBM Plex Sans and
  Atkinson Hyperlegible Next) plus the fonts installed on your system. Text size now
  scales every font.
- **Connection** (formerly Servers) installs, starts, stops and removes the daemon and
  the notifier as systemd user services on Linux, with an optional "Start on login".
  The app can then connect to the local daemon. Installing real systemd units has only
  been tested with a simulated systemd so far.
- **API keys** use plain-language permission names, "Read only" and "Everything" quick
  picks, and expiry presets.
- On a phone held sideways, Settings fills the screen.

## Main window

- The account status dot stays green whatever your accent colour, with a subtle pulse
  (off when reduced motion is on).
- Borders are drawn once, and message tabs share the reader's header row.
- The loading screen shows the logo straight away and fades out smoothly.

## Extensions

- **Extension bus:** with the new `extensions.bus` capability, extensions send each
  other requests and events by name. Built-in parts of the app take part too: an
  extension can add composer buttons, read or change the draft, add banners to or
  change how a message is shown, react when a message is opened or selected, and show
  notifications. See the
  [bus contract](https://github.com/hexvale-labs/colecto/blob/v0.3.0/docs/extensions/README.md#extension-bus).
- **Extension settings:** an extension can declare toggles, sliders, choices and text
  fields. You change them in Settings → Extensions, and the extension reads them.
  Oneko uses this for speed, opacity and stopping distance.
- **Rust SDK:** the new `colecto-extension` crate lets you write an extension as plain
  Rust functions, with typed mail calls, typed bus messages whose names are checked
  when you compile, and a mock host for `cargo test`. Extensions need no `unsafe` code.
- **`cargo colecto`:** builds, checks and packages a Rust extension in one step. It
  catches mistakes that would otherwise just fail silently, such as handling an event
  the manifest does not subscribe to, and prints the fix.
- Both are installed from this release's tag; see the
  [Rust SDK guide](https://github.com/hexvale-labs/colecto/blob/v0.3.0/docs/extensions/rust-sdk.md).
  Oneko is now written with the SDK.
- Installing an extension whose ID is already taken is refused.

## Self-hosting

- `GET /api/v1/version` and `colecto-daemon --version` report the version and the Git
  commit the build came from. See
  [self-hosting](https://github.com/hexvale-labs/colecto/blob/v0.3.0/docs/self-hosting.md).

## Downloads and limits

Downloads are the same as in v0.2.0 (Linux `.deb`, `.rpm`, `.AppImage`; Windows `.exe`
and `.msi`; Android `.apk`) and are still not code-signed; see
[installing](https://github.com/hexvale-labs/colecto/blob/v0.3.0/docs/install.md). The
[known limits](https://github.com/hexvale-labs/colecto/blob/v0.3.0/docs/roadmap.md)
still apply, and storage formats may change between alpha versions.
